title: Morphing Geometry with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that displays a morphing 3D geometry with a toggleable physics debug overlay. Detailed requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (color: 0x0a0a1a)
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.5) and a point light (0xffffff, intensity 1.5) at (5, 8, 5)
- A ground plane (20x20) at y=0 with a dark grid material (0x222244), visible but subtle

## Main Morphing Object
- Create a central mesh that morphs between 4 shapes: Sphere (radius 1.5), Box (2x2x2), Torus (radius 1.2, tube 0.5), and Icosahedron (radius 1.5)
- The object floats at y=2.5 and has a wireframe + solid dual-render (solid mesh with 0x00aaff emissive material, plus a wireframe overlay in 0x00ffcc)
- Morphing is triggered by pressing keys 1-4 (1=Sphere, 2=Box, 3=Torus, 4=Icosahedron)
- When morphing, smoothly interpolate the geometry vertices over 1 second using a lerp. During morph, the object should glow brighter (increase emissive intensity)
- Track the current shape index (0-3) and morph progress (0.0 to 1.0)

## Physics Simulation
- Simulate simple gravity-based particle physics: when the shape morphs, emit 20 particles from the surface that fall with gravity (g = -9.8) and bounce once off the ground plane with restitution 0.4
- Particles are small spheres (radius 0.05) colored to match the wireframe color, with lifetime of 3 seconds
- Track total active particle count

## Physics Debug Overlay
- Toggle with key 'D': a debug overlay that shows:
  - Wireframe bounding box around the main object (yellow, 0xffff00)
  - Velocity vectors on active particles (as small line segments, red 0xff0000)
  - A text label showing the bounding box dimensions near the object
- The debug overlay has 3 states: 'off', 'wireframe', 'full' (cycle through with D key)
  - 'off': no debug visuals
  - 'wireframe': only bounding box
  - 'full': bounding box + velocity vectors + text labels

## HUD / DOM Elements
- Top-left HUD panel (CSS overlay, semi-transparent black background, id='hud-panel'):
  - Current shape name (id='shape-name')
  - Morph progress bar (id='morph-progress', a div that fills width 0-100%)
  - Active particle count (id='particle-count')
  - Debug mode label (id='debug-mode')
  - FPS counter (id='fps-counter')
- Bottom-center: 4 clickable buttons (ids: 'btn-sphere', 'btn-box', 'btn-torus', 'btn-icosa') that also trigger morphs
- A toggle button (id='btn-debug') that cycles debug overlay mode

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- currentShapeIndex: number (0=Sphere, 1=Box, 2=Torus, 3=Icosahedron)
- targetShapeIndex: number (the shape being morphed to)
- morphProgress: number (0.0 when idle at a shape, 0.0-1.0 during transition, snaps to 0.0 when done)
- isMorphing: boolean
- activeParticleCount: number
- debugMode: string ('off' | 'wireframe' | 'full')
- objectPosition: {x, y, z} of the main mesh
- boundingBoxSize: {x, y, z} dimensions of the bounding box
- totalMorphCount: number (how many morph transitions have been triggered)
- fps: number (current FPS)
- particleSystemActive: boolean (true if any particles exist)
- groundPlaneVisible: boolean

## Animation
- The main object slowly rotates on Y axis (0.3 rad/s) continuously
- Particles update each frame with Euler integration
- Morph interpolation uses smooth easing (ease-in-out)
physics_constraints: Particles fall under gravity g=-9.8 m/s², bounce off ground (y=0) with restitution coefficient 0.4. Particles have 3-second lifetime. Bounding box must accurately reflect current geometry dimensions during morph. Morph interpolation must complete in exactly 1 second.
